meta.title: METHODOLOGY
meta.subtitle: How the Non-Firm Power Insurance Risk Index is built

blocks.text: Score an unscored population on a disciplined rubric, ship it clean and downloadable, and stay honest about what is measured versus assessed.

The UK is connecting data centres and grid-scale assets on terms that are increasingly not firm — interruptible, curtailable, or contingent on a connection queue that now runs to triple-digit gigawatts.{{cite:NESO-TEC,OFGEM-DEMAND-REFORM}} The financial consequence is breached SLAs and lost revenue, not physical damage. This page documents how we score {{fact:total}} market participants on Exposure versus Preparedness, fuse register readings with sourced research, and grade the harness before anything is published as measurement.

Every entity carries two axis scores on 0–100 before any single headline number: Exposure (the size of the non-firm bet) and Preparedness (the ability to carry it). Each axis is a weighted sum of five sub-factors rated 0–4, rescaled to 0–100. Scoring is arithmetic in code (harness/scoring.py) — never an LLM free-text opinion.

The axis score is E = (Σ wi · reff,i / 4) × 100 (and likewise P on the preparedness side): a weighted average of effective sub-factor ratings, where each reff fuses a register reading with a research reading (below). Margin of Safety = P − E — the surplus of preparedness over exposure. Quadrant cut-lines are in-sample medians on the live universe (currently exp ≥ {{fact:cut_exp}}, prep ≥ {{fact:cut_prep}}), not fixed 50/50 — so the index ranks relative firmness-risk and re-centres as the universe grows.

blocks.text: Each sub-factor can carry two ratings: a deterministic rating from a register or filing, and a latent rating from sourced research. The effective rating is a credibility-weighted blend{{cite:ACT-CREDIBILITY}} — reff = clamp( λ·rdet + (1−λ)·rlat ) — where λ is set by the evidence tier of the deterministic input.

blocks.text: Non-firm power risk lives across a value chain and a rulebook. We score four entity layers plus a fifth rules feed that re-prices firmness when regulation changes — the same in-force discipline as a live regulatory product.

blocks.caption: Entity layers in the index universe

items.name: Carriers & syndicates
items.role: Hold the balance sheet. Exposure is energy / DC premium concentration; preparedness is capital, products, and curtailment pricing expertise.

items.name: MGAs & brokers
items.role: Price and place without mostly carrying the balance sheet. Exposure is risk routed through facilities; preparedness is products they can structure.

items.name: Energy & data-centre assets
items.role: Originate the peril. Exposure is flexible-connection share and queue position from NESO TEC Gate column and DNO ECR flexible flags; preparedness is backup and monitoring.
items.examples: Hyperscale campuses, batteries on Gate-1 / curtailable connections

items.name: Reinsurers & capacity
items.role: Stand behind carriers. Exposure is correlated tail across cedants; preparedness is rated capital and correlation modelling.

items.name: Rules feed
items.role: In-force CUSC / Grid Code mods and NESO/Ofgem decisions. Defines what firm legally means; flags records for re-score.

blocks.caption: In-force rules that re-price firmness on the live index.

blocks.text: The build is a directed pipeline over the shared contract, but what perfects the data is a set of named loops — each with a trigger, an input, an output, and an exit criterion (METHODOLOGY §6). Nothing synthetic enters the scored universe; LLM research fills qualitative gaps only.

steps.title: Ingestion loop
steps.detail: ingest_live.py — NESO TEC + DNO ECR pulls; diff Gate status and in-force rules.

steps.title: Scoring + linking
steps.detail: score_and_validate.py — fuse latent × deterministic; propagate L3 firmness to carriers; recompute median cuts.

steps.title: Eval / drift (L0–L8)
steps.detail: evals.py — golden-set drift, weight sums, reproducibility; L5 is the publication gate.

steps.title: Validation / adversary
steps.detail: industry_stress.py + verify_methodology.py — sourcing audits, model-spec sync, contract alignment.

steps.title: Publication gate
steps.detail: publication_gate.py — blended measured/disclosed share must clear 60%; currently {{fact:measured_pct}} on {{fact:total}} entities.

blocks.text: The index stays PROVISIONAL until blended measured/disclosed share reaches 60% (L5). At {{fact:measured_pct}} on {{fact:total}} entities the direction of each score is defensible; magnitudes firm up as register tiers land. This section reflects the live universe on each build — not a stale eval report. Per-entity drill-down shows each rating's provenance.

Three preparedness sub-factors — data & monitoring, underwriting expertise, pricing & modelling — rest on judgement by nature, so the measurable load sits mostly on the exposure axis where registers and filings carry the weight.
The harness grades itself L0–L8 on every build. L5 is the publication gate; L6 checks axis weight sums; L8 is full reproducibility from records through to the static site.

blocks.text: Every sub-factor maps to a named primary source — a connection register, statutory filing, rating, or filed wording — with the exact field recorded in the harness. No value is a model guess dressed as a measurement.

items.name: NESO TEC register
items.what: Transmission Entry Capacity — which gate an asset sits behind. Share of MW on Gate 1 signals non-firm status.

items.name: DNO Embedded Capacity Registers
items.what: Per-DNO embedded connections; MW-weighted share flagged with flexible / curtailable connection terms.
items.field: Opendatasoft v2.1 · import capacity × flexible-connection flag

items.name: Grid geography (ECR / TEC + NESO boundaries)
items.what: Location fields and NESO constraint boundaries reduced to a Herfindahl concentration of covered MW.

items.name: Companies House / SFCR
items.what: iXBRL statutory accounts and segmental disclosure; Solvency II SCR coverage.

items.name: AM Best / S&P / Fitch FSR
items.what: Financial-strength rating mapped with SCR coverage to a 0–4 capital rating by fixed lookup.

items.name: FCA Financial Services Register
items.what: Approved-persons and permissions data — named specialist function, not a press claim.

items.name: Filed product wordings
items.what: Filed wordings and Lloyd's binding-authority classes — whether availability / parametric cover exists.
